subtitle: Blessings on lightning, earthquakes, and natural phenomena; theodicy and divine justice
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's commentary on Tractate Berakhot — the laws of the Shema, daily prayers, Grace after Meals, and blessings on food and wonders. Original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic with English translation.

aligned.en: "And *zeva'ot*" — a rumbling heard in the air resembling a millstone turning with shafts upon a second millstone.

aligned.ja: וקולה פי אלג'באל ואלכדאה ומא בעדהא ברוך עושה בראשית לא גיר. אמא אלמתקדמה מת'ל אלשהב ואלריאח אלעאצפה ומא ד'כר בינהמא פיבארך ברוך עושה בראשית או ברוך שכוחו מלא עולם.
aligned.en: His statement regarding mountains, hills, and what follows them is "Blessed is He who makes the work of creation" and nothing else. But over the preceding phenomena — such as the shooting stars, the violent winds, and what was mentioned between them — one blesses either "Blessed is He who makes the work of creation" or "Blessed is He whose power and might fill the world."

pairs.en: mountains, hills
Blessed is He who makes the work of creation
shooting stars, the violent winds
Blessed is He whose power and might fill the world

aligned.ja: וקול ר' יהודה לפרקים יריד בה אד'א ראה בעד מדה, וד'לך מן ת'לאת'ין יומא אלי ת'לאת'ין יומא פמא זאד. והלכה כר' יהודה.
aligned.en: The statement of Rabbi Yehudah, "from time to time" (*li-feraqim*), means: when one sees it after an interval, that being from thirty days to thirty days; but beyond that [no further blessing is required]. And the law is according to Rabbi Yehudah.

pairs.en: Rabbi Yehudah
*li-feraqim*

pairs.ja: מן ת'לאת'ין יומא אלי ת'לאת'ין יומא

aligned.ja: משנה [ג]
aligned.en: Mishnah [3]

aligned.ja: קולה על הרעה מעין על הטובה ועל הטובה מעין על הרעה, יריד בה אנה אד'א נזלת בה נאזלהֵ שר ועלי אן עאקבתהא כ'יר יבארך ברוך דיין האמת, והד'א הו מעין הרעה.
aligned.en: His statement "over the evil as over the good, and over the good as over the evil" means the following: when some misfortune befalls a person, yet its outcome is good, he blesses "Blessed is the true Judge" — and this is "[blessing over the good] as over the evil."

pairs.en: over the evil as over the good

pairs.ja: נאזלהֵ שר ועלי אן עאקבתהא כ'יר
pairs.en: misfortune befalls a person, yet its outcome is good
Blessed is the true Judge

aligned.ja: וכד'לך איצ'א אד'א אנג'ר לה כ'יר ועלי אן עאקבהֵ ד'לך שר יבארך ברוך הטוב והמטיב, והד'א הו מעין הטובה.
aligned.en: Likewise, when some good is drawn to him, yet its outcome is evil, he blesses "Blessed is the good and beneficent One" — and this is "[blessing over the evil] as over the good."

pairs.ja: אנג'ר לה כ'יר ועלי אן עאקבהֵ ד'לך שר
pairs.en: some good is drawn to him, yet its outcome is evil
Blessed is the good and beneficent One
as over the good

aligned.ja: ומת'אל אלקצה אלאולי אן יג'וז אלסיל עלי ארצ'ה, פד'לך שר, ואן אעקב כ'ירא לאן תרוי אלארץ' בה וקד רב מא יג'לב ד'לך אלסיל לארצ'ה פואיד.
aligned.en: An example of the first case: a torrent passes over his land — that is an evil — yet it issues in good, for the land is watered by it, and often that torrent brings benefits to his land.

pairs.en: the first case
torrent passes over his land
the land is watered by it
torrent brings benefits to his land

aligned.ja: ומת'אל אלקצה אלת'אניה אן יג'ד מאלא ויראה אכ'ר ענד ד'לך, פד'לך כ'יר, ועלי אן עאקבהֵ ד'לך שר, לאן ד'לך אלד'י ראה ינם בה לאלמלך ויעד'בה ויטלב מנה אכת'ר ממא וג'ד.
aligned.en: An example of the second case: he finds money, and at that moment another person sees him — that is a good — yet its outcome is evil, for the one who saw him informs the king of it, who then torments him and demands of him more than he found.

pairs.en: the second case
he finds money, and another person sees him
informs the king of it
demands of him more than he found

aligned.ja: ועלהֵ הד'א אלפקה אן אלאשיא אלחאצ'רה הי אלתי ליס פי וג'ודהא שך, פיבארך עלי מא הי עליה ולא ינט'ר לעואקבהא, לאן תלך אלעואקב ממכנה, וכפי באלממכן כונה ממכן.
aligned.en: The reason for this ruling is that present things are those in whose existence there is no doubt, so one blesses over them as they actually are and does not look to their outcomes, since those outcomes are merely possible, and for a possible thing it suffices to be possible.

pairs.en: present things
in whose existence there is no doubt
does not look to their outcomes
those outcomes are merely possible

aligned.ja: שרח לשעבר אלמאצ'י, לאן לא ידעי לאללה פי מא קד אנקצ'י, ואנמא ידעי אללה ויטלב מנה אלאמור אלממכנה פי אלמסתקבל.
aligned.en: The explanation of *le-she'avar* is "the past," for one does not petition God concerning what has already elapsed; rather, one petitions God and asks of Him concerning possible matters in the future.

pairs.en: explanation of *le-she'avar*
the past

pairs.ja: לא ידעי לאללה פי מא קד אנקצ'י
pairs.en: does not petition God concerning what has already elapsed
possible matters in the future

aligned.ja: משנה [ד]
aligned.en: Mishnah [4]

aligned.ja: כרך, אלמדינה. וקולה הנא מתפלל, ליס יריד בה לא צלאה באסתקבאל קבלה ותאהב, ולא איצ'א ברכה, ואנמא הו דעא, ענד אלדכ'ול ידעו אן יסלמה אללה פי הד'ה אלמדינה, וענד כ'רוג'ה מנהא ישכר אללה אלד'י כ'לצה פיהא.
aligned.en: "*Kerakh*" — the city. His statement here, "he prays," does not mean that one should pray facing the *qiblah* with formal preparation, nor a blessing either; rather it is a supplication: upon entering, he prays that God deliver him safely in this city, and upon leaving it, he gives thanks to God who delivered him within it.

pairs.en: *Kerakh* — the city
not pray facing the *qiblah*

pairs.ja: ענד אלדכ'ול ידעו אן יסלמה אללה
pairs.en: upon entering, he prays that God deliver him
upon leaving it, he gives thanks to God

aligned.ja: ובן עזאי יזיד את'נתין, ענד אלדכ'ול איצ'א ישכר אללה עלי מא כ'לצה פי אלטריק אלי אן וצל סאלמא לאלמדינה, וענד כ'רוג'ה מנהא ידעו אללה אן יכ'לצה איצ'א פי אלטריק אלתי יסלכהא.
aligned.en: And Ben Azzai adds two more: upon entering, he also gives thanks to God for having delivered him on the road until he arrived safely at the city, and upon leaving it, he prays to God to deliver him likewise on the road that he will travel.

pairs.en: Ben Azzai adds two more

pairs.ja: ישכר אללה עלי מא כ'לצה פי אלטריק
pairs.en: gives thanks to God for having delivered him on the road
arrived safely at the city

pairs.ja: ידעו אללה אן יכ'לצה פי אלטריק
pairs.en: prays to God to deliver him on the road

aligned.ja: וקד קאל לך מלאך הד'א אלאמר והו אן ישכר אללה עלי מא אנעם בה פי אלמאצ'י, ויטלב מנה אן ינעם עליה פי אלמסתקבל. והלכה כבן עזאי.
aligned.en: The angel has already taught you this matter — namely, that one give thanks to God for the favor He bestowed in the past, and ask of Him to bestow favor upon him in the future. And the law is according to Ben Azzai.

pairs.en: The angel has already taught you this matter

pairs.ja: ישכר אללה עלי מא אנעם בה פי אלמאצ'י
pairs.en: give thanks to God for the favor He bestowed in the past

pairs.ja: ויטלב מנה אן ינעם עליה פי אלמסתקבל
pairs.en: ask of Him to bestow favor upon him in the future
the law is according to Ben Azzai

aligned.ja: משנה [ה]
aligned.en: Mishnah [5]

aligned.ja: קולה כשם שהוא מברך על הטובה, יריד בה אן יקבל ד'לך בסרור ויקהר טביעתה ויבסט נפסה ענד מא יבארך ברוך דיין האמת, חתי יכון מת'ל וקת יבארך ברוך הטוב והמטיב, וכמא יקולון אלחכמים פי אכת'ר כלאמהם כל מה דעביד משמיא לטב.
aligned.en: His statement "just as he blesses over the good" means that one should receive it with joy, subduing his nature and composing his soul when he blesses "Blessed is the true Judge," so that it be as at the moment he blesses "Blessed is the good and beneficent One" — as the Sages say in most of their discourse, "Everything the Heavens do is for the good" (BT Berakhot 60b).

pairs.en: just as he blesses over the good
receive it with joy, subduing his nature
Blessed is the true Judge
Blessed is the good and beneficent One
Everything the Heavens do is for the good

aligned.ja: והד'א אמר עקלי ענד אלעקלא ולו לם יחץ' עליה אלשרע, לאן אשיא כת'ירה יט'ן בהא שרא פי אולהא ויכון מאלהא אלי כ'יר כת'יר, ואשיא כת'ירה יט'ן בהא פי אולהא כ'ירא ויכון פי אכ'רהא שר עט'ים.
aligned.en: This is a rational matter in the view of the intelligent, even were the Law not to urge it, for many things are supposed at their outset to be evil and yet their end is much good, while many things are supposed at their outset to be good and yet at their end is great evil.

pairs.en: a rational matter in the view of the intelligent
even were the Law not to urge it

pairs.ja: יט'ן בהא שרא פי אולהא ויכון מאלהא אלי כ'יר
pairs.en: supposed at their outset to be evil and yet their end is much good

pairs.ja: יט'ן בהא פי אולהא כ'ירא ויכון פי אכ'רהא שר עט'ים
pairs.en: supposed at their outset to be good and yet at their end is great evil

aligned.ja: פלד'לך לא יג'ב לאלעאקל אן יכאב ענד נזול אפה עט'ימהֵ אלקדר ודאהיה שניעהֵ אלכ'טר, אד' לא יעלם אלמאל. ולא איצ'א ינכ'דע ויסר אלסרור אלכאמל ענד מא ינג'ר לה כ'יר בזעמה, לאנה לא יעלם אלמאל.
aligned.en: Therefore the intelligent person ought not be cast down when a calamity of grave magnitude or a dreadful, perilous misfortune descends upon him, since he does not know its end. Nor, on the other hand, ought he be deceived and rejoice with complete joy when some good is drawn to him by his reckoning, for he does not know its end.

pairs.en: the intelligent person ought not be cast down
calamity of grave magnitude
he does not know its end
ought he be deceived and rejoice with complete joy

aligned.ja: וכד'לך חרמוא עליהם אלסלאם אלתגאיי פי אלפרח ואלצ'חך, אללהם אלא אן כאן ד'לך אלפרח באמר עלוי אעני אמתת'אל אלכ'יר וטלבה. ואמא אלנהי ען אלחזן ואלאכתיאב פהו מן אלשהרה פי כתב אלנבוה פי חיז לא יתכלם פיה.
aligned.en: So too the Sages, peace be upon them, prohibited excess in joy and laughter — unless that joy be over an exalted matter, I mean compliance with the good and the seeking of it. As for the prohibition against grief and dejection, it is famous in the books of prophecy, within a domain that is not to be discussed here.

pairs.ja: חרמוא עליהם אלסלאם אלתגאיי פי אלפרח ואלצ'חך
pairs.en: the Sages, peace be upon them, prohibited excess in joy and laughter
joy be over an exalted matter
compliance with the good and the seeking of it
prohibition against grief and dejection
books of prophecy

aligned.ja: והד'א אן לם יכן ד'לך אלאמר כ'יר פי אלדניא מן אולה אלי אכ'רה ויזעם אלזאעם אנה קד סעד ופאז, ותלך אלסעאדה אלמט'נונה כאנת אלסבב לתמנעה אלסעאדה אלחקיקיה, ויכון ד'לך סבב לטרדו מן חיי עולם הבא, ופי מת'ל ד'לך קאל יש דרך ישר לפני איש ואחריתה דרכי מות.
aligned.en: This holds even if that matter not be good in this world from its beginning to its end, and the claimant claims that he has prospered and triumphed — yet that supposed felicity was the cause that barred him from true felicity, and became a cause for his expulsion from the life of the World to Come. Of the like of this it is said, "There is a way that seems straight before a man, but its end is the ways of death" (Prov 14:12).

pairs.en: supposed felicity
barred him from true felicity
expulsion from the life of the World to Come

pairs.ja: יש דרך ישר לפני איש ואחריתה דרכי מות
pairs.en: There is a way that seems straight before a man, but its end is the ways of death

aligned.ja: פלד'לך יקצד אלאנסאן בפכרה וידעו אללה אן יג'על ג'מיע מא יצלה פי אלדניא מן שרורהא וכ'יראתהא סבבא לניל אלסעאדה אלחקיקיה.
aligned.en: Therefore a person should aim, in his thought, and petition God to make all that reaches him in this world — of its evils and its goods — a cause for attaining true felicity.

pairs.en: a person should aim, in his thought
petition God to make
its evils and its goods
a cause for attaining true felicity

aligned.ja: וקולה ביצר טוב וביצר רע, יעני אן יכ'טר בבאלה חב אללה ואעתקאדה ולו פי חאל אלעציאן ואלחרג' ואלגצ'ב אלד'י ד'לך כלה יצר רע, מת'ל קולהם בכל דרכיך דעהו ואפילו בדבר עבירה.
aligned.en: His statement "with the good inclination and the evil inclination" means that one should bring to mind the love of God and faith in Him even in a state of disobedience, distress, and anger — all of which is the evil inclination — as in their saying "In all your ways know Him" (Prov 3:6), "even in a matter of transgression" (BT Berakhot 63a).

pairs.en: with the good inclination and the evil inclination
the love of God and faith in Him
a state of disobedience, distress, and anger
In all your ways know Him
even in a matter of transgression

aligned.ja: ושרח מדה, טריקה, יעני פי אי חאלה אחלך סבחה ואשכרה.
aligned.en: The explanation of *middah* is "a path," meaning: in whatever state, I make Him sweet to me and give Him thanks.

pairs.en: explanation of *middah*
a path
in whatever state
I make Him sweet to me and give Him thanks

aligned.ja: משנה [ו]
aligned.en: Mishnah [6]

aligned.ja: קלות ראש, צ'ד כובד ראש אלמתקדם, ומענאה אן לא ינהמך פי אלצ'חך ואללהו ואלטרב.
aligned.en: "*Qalut rosh*" (levity) — the opposite of the *koved rosh* (gravity) mentioned earlier; its meaning is that one should not plunge into laughter, frivolity, and merrymaking.

pairs.en: *Qalut rosh*
*koved rosh* mentioned earlier

pairs.ja: לא ינהמך פי אלצ'חך ואללהו ואלטרב
pairs.en: not plunge into laughter, frivolity, and merrymaking

aligned.ja: ושער המזרח, יריד בה אלבאב אלשרקי מן אבואב אלעזרה, והו אלמשהור בשער ניקנור. וקדש הקדשים פי גרב אלעזרה מקבאל ד'לך אלבאב.
aligned.en: "And the eastern gate" (*sha'ar ha-mizraḥ*) — by this he means the eastern gate among the gates of the Temple Court (*ʿazarah*), which is the one known as the Gate of Nicanor. And the Holy of Holies is at the west of the Court, facing that gate.

pairs.en: *sha'ar ha-mizraḥ*
the eastern gate among the gates of the Temple Court
Gate of Nicanor
Holy of Holies is at the west of the Court

aligned.ja: ושרח מכוון, מואזיא. ומקלו, עצאה. ואפונדתו, ת'וב ילבסה אלאנסאן לג'סמה כי יערק פיה ולא תתמרת' ת'יאבה אלרפיעה באלערק, וליס מן שאן אחד אן יכ'רג' בה וחדה אלי אן ילבס עליה ת'וב אכ'ר.
aligned.en: The explanation of *mekhuvvan* is "aligned, directly opposite." And *maqlo* is "his staff." And *afundato* is a garment a person wears against his body so that he may sweat in it and his fine garments not be soiled with sweat; and it is not proper for anyone to go out wearing it alone until he puts another garment over it.

pairs.en: explanation of *mekhuvvan* is "aligned, directly opposite"
*maqlo* is "his staff"
*afundato*

pairs.ja: ת'וב ילבסה אלאנסאן לג'סמה כי יערק
pairs.en: a garment a person wears against his body so that he may sweat
his fine garments not be soiled with sweat

aligned.ja: ושרח קפנדריא, אן יג'עלה טריק ליקרב אלמסאפה, וד'לך באן ידכ'ל עלי באב ויכ'רג' עלי באב ת'אן יקאבלה ליצל למוצ'ע מא, לאן לא יג'וז אן ידכ'ל ד'לך אלג'בל אלמכרם עלי אול אלחאל אלא לוג'ה מן וג'וה אלתעבד.
aligned.en: The explanation of *qappandarya* is that one make [the Temple Mount] a passage to shorten the distance — namely, that he enter by one gate and exit by another opposite it in order to reach some place; for it is not permitted to enter that honored mount in the first instance except for one of the purposes of worship.

pairs.en: explanation of *qappandarya*
make [the Temple Mount] a passage to shorten the distance

pairs.ja: ידכ'ל עלי באב ויכ'רג' עלי באב ת'אן
pairs.en: enter by one gate and exit by another opposite it
that honored mount

aligned.ja: וקולה ורקיקה מקל וחומר, שרחה אן יחרם אלבזאק פי ד'לך אלג'בל בטריק אלאחרי ואלאג'דר, לאן אד'א כאן אלנעל אלד'י עמל לאלציאנה לאנה יצון אלרג'ל יחרם אן ידכ'ל בה ד'לך אלג'בל, פבאלחרי ואלאג'דר אן תחרם אלבזקה פיה אלתי הי שי מסתקד'ר.
aligned.en: His statement "and spitting follows by an *a fortiori* inference (*qal va-ḥomer*)" — its explanation is that spitting is forbidden on that mount by an *a fortiori* and all the more fitting inference: for if the sandal, which is made for protection — since it protects the foot — yet one is forbidden to enter that mount with it, then all the more fitting and proper is it that spitting be forbidden there, it being something repugnant.

aligned.ja: ושרח קלקלו, אפסדוא, יעני אפסדוא אלאעתקאדאת. ולמא ד'כר מן ג'מלהֵ אלתקנות אנהם רתבוא אן יסלם באסם אללה לאן שלום מן אסמא אללה ג'עלוה, אכ'ד' אן יסתדל עלי כון ד'לך ג'איז מן בעז אלד'י קאל ה' עמכם וג'אובוה הם יברכך ה'.
aligned.en: The explanation of *qilqelu* is "they corrupted" — meaning they corrupted the beliefs. Since he mentioned, among the ordinances (*taqqanot*), that they instituted that one greet his fellow with the name of God — for "Peace" (*Shalom*) they reckoned to be among the names of God — he proceeds to adduce a proof that this is permissible from Boaz, who said "The Lord be with you," and they answered him "The Lord bless you" (Ruth 2:4).

aligned.en: His subsequent statement "And it says, 'Do not despise your mother when she is old'" (Prov 23:22) is not a proof for the foregoing — namely his statement "that a person may inquire after the welfare of his fellow with the name [of God]" — rather it is an adducing of proof that one must not make light of the ordinances of the Sages even if they are ancient and the time of that ordinance is long past; and to this Solomon urged by this parable.

aligned.en: This subject is long and far-reaching — "deep, deep, who can find it out?" (Eccl 7:24) — for in it we are led to the question of [divine] decree and foreordination. So do not seek of me, in the matter I am now treating, anything but the setting forth of the words of the theologians only, by way of explaining the plain sense of the wording — for the scriptural texts have contradicted one another greatly on this, and likewise the statements of the Sages.

aligned.ja: לכן אלקאעדה אן אללה יג'אזי אלמחסנין ויעאקב אלמסיין, וד'לך עדל מנה, לאנה שהד עלי נפסה באלעדל פי אלכל כי כל דרכיו משפט וכו'. ווג'ה אלעדל פי ד'לך ליס פי טאקהֵ אלאנסאן אלאדראך לה, כמא ליס פי קוהֵ אלעקול אלאדמיה אלאחאטה במערפתה תעלי.
aligned.en: But the principle is that God rewards the well-doers and punishes the evildoers, and that is justice on His part, for He has testified concerning Himself to justice in all, "for all His ways are justice" (Deut 32:4), and so forth. The aspect of justice in this is not within a human being's capacity to grasp, just as it is not within the power of human intellects to encompass knowledge of Him, exalted be He.
